title: progressive-traffic-fence-with-kv-lease-circuit-and-stream-quiesce
creator: Asha Mirza
description: Implement a progressive active-active traffic fencing mechanism that uses per-session KV leases and a stepwise circuit to shift traffic between regions without breaking streaming sessions. This ticket covers the control-plane policy, runtime lease semantics, and operational runbook for gradual traffic fencing and automated rollback when SLO regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Can shift up to 100% of stateless traffic across regions in 5% increments with no more than 1% increase in 95th-percentile latency for unaffected sessions
Streaming sessions are quiesced and migrated with less than 2s of observable input loss in 99% of test repro scenarios
Circuit breaker trips and automatic rollback occur when regional error budget consumption exceeds configured thresholds (default: 50% of budget in 1 hour)
Telemetry emits region-level moving averages for token burn rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, outstanding session count, and KV lease contention metrics
Smoke and chaos tests pass in staging (see links) and rollout playbook documented in Confluence
comments: 2025-02-18 - Asha Mirza: Initial ticket created after oncall postmortem showed repeated region thrash during scheduled maintenance. Proposed hybrid approach: per-session KV lease to indicate active region + a staged traffic fence controlled by a policy engine.

2025-02-20 - Diego Park: Spike complete. Implemented KV lease prototype (lease_id, owner_region, ttl_ms, seq) and a lease-refresh handshake for streaming session owners. Observations: short-ttl (5s) causes excessive churn under moderate packet loss; switching to jittered 15s TTL with paced refreshes reduces churn.

2025-02-24 - Design review (Lena Schultz): Reviewed UX impacts for Console rollouts. Need explicit user-visible 'in-flight session count' and an emergency 'drain now' toggle. Also recommended exposing circuit state (OPEN/HALF_OPEN/CLOSED) per route in Console.

2025-02-26 - Diego Park: Implemented traffic-fence controller that increments regional weights in 5% steps with a configurable pause (default 60s) between steps. Controller observes moving-average p99 latency and token burn; will pause or step back if thresholds exceeded.

2025-02-27 - QA (Jamal Nguyen): Integration tests added for gRPC streaming. Found a corner where multi-subrequest sessions that multiplex over a single websocket had prefix cache invalidation during handoff. Mitigation: mark multi-subrequest sessions as 'sticky' and require KV lease ownership transfer before routing change.

2025-03-01 - Diego Park: Added circuit-breaker variant that calculates a 'regional stress score' composed of: error_rate(5m)*3 + p99_latency_delta(5m) + session_eviction_rate. If score > 7, circuit goes HALF_OPEN and pauses fence increments. Rules are tunable per-tenant.

2025-03-02 - SRE (Marta Koh): Runbook draft uploaded. Key actions: (1) pause fence at current step, (2) enable emergency drain to new region, (3) scale dedicated capacity, (4) open mute on telemetry to reduce noise. Added automatic rollback trigger when error budget used > 60% in 30m.

2025-03-03 - Diego Park: PR #3489 created. Implementation covers controller, KV lease API endpoints, per-session state flagging, Console telemetry hooks, and an e2e test harness. Still pending security review for lease token signing + KMS integration.

2025-03-04 - Product (Rae Thompson): Confirmed customer-facing constraints: enterprise customers can opt-out of automatic fencing and require manual approval. Added label and UI requirement to Console items.

2025-03-04 - Diego Park: Next steps: complete KMS-backed lease signing (blocked), finalize PR comments, schedule canary deployment to us-west-2/staging and run chaos simulation of control-plane partition. Target canary date: 2025-03-11.
design_decisions: Use per-session KV lease rather than global session table to reduce cross-region coordination under normal operation
Stepwise weight adjustments (5% increments) to limit blast radius and make rollback granular
Combine moving-average latency and token-burn to determine stress rather than relying solely on error rates
Mark multi-multiplexed sessions as sticky to avoid prefix-caching anomalies during transfer
Expose circuit state and fence progress in Console for operator visibility
test_plan: Unit tests for KV lease refresh/expiry semantics
Integration tests for streaming handoff: simulate packet drops and control-plane delays
Chaos test: simulate full region outage and observe automatic incremental fence + rollback behavior
Load test: verify p50/p95/p99 delta stays within acceptance during 5%-to-100% migration under 2x baseline load
Canary in staging across us-west-2 and eu-central-1 with synthetic streaming clients (1k concurrent)
rollout_plan: 2) Deploy controller and KV-lease service to staging, run canary tests
3) Enable progressive fence on non-critical routes (5% starting) in staging
4) Run chaos-simulated control-plane partition and observe behavior
5) Promote to production for low-traffic tenant segment, monitor for 24h
6) Gradually expand to 50% of traffic across regions; if stable, enable enterprise collections with opt-out compliance
7) Full production rollout with SRE on-call and rollback playbook ready
monitoring_and_slos: p99 latency target for hosted API: < 350ms (regional baseline)
Error budget policy: consume < 0.05% errors tokenized over request volume per region per day
Key signals: kv_lease_contention_ratio, fence_step_back_count, regional_stress_score, streaming_input_loss_rate
Alerts: auto-pause fence when regional_stress_score > 7 for > 5m or kv_lease_contention_ratio > 0.1
rollback_criteria: Immediate rollback if customer errors increase by > 3x baseline for > 10m
Rollback if streaming_input_loss_rate breach persists for > 5m at > 0.5% of sessions
Rollback if SLO error budget exceeds configured threshold during migration window
